_doc: Maps calculator asset-class keys (broker_ibkr.json keys) to harness instrument selectors. Two forms are accepted. (1) A LIST of instrument-key patterns, matched against `_instrument_key(df)` from quality/analyze.py, which produces '<symbol>/<secType>' or '<symbol>/<secType>/<expiry>'; '*' is an fnmatch wildcard. (2) An OBJECT with any of `patterns`, `exchange_any`, `currency_any` — every key present must hold. Form 2 exists because the EU classes partition by VENUE and the instrument key carries no venue; see `_venue_partitioned`.
_edit_authority: ⚑ THIS FILE IS READ-ONLY TO EVERY AGENT (hq CLAUDE.md convention 8). The
2026-08-11 edit to the three EU selectors was made by Claude Code under
Marcel's EXPLICIT per-edit authorisation, asked for and given in session.
It is not a precedent and does not amend the convention, which is his to
amend (0b vii). Read the git history that way.
What made it the mildest instance of the rule: the rule exists because
hand-editing a MEASURED value is the assumed-spread failure S1-33 forbids.
The values added are venue codes read off each contract's own
`validExchanges` from IBKR, not numbers anyone chose. `broker_ibkr.json`
was NOT touched — those are rates, and the live batch measures them.
_venue_partitioned: EU_STK_XETRA, EU_STK_LSE and EU_STK_SIX are the same secType on three
different venues. `_instrument_key` is '<symbol>/<secType>', so it cannot
tell them apart and a symbol-only pattern for one would match a listing on
either of the others. Hence `exchange_any` / `currency_any`.
⚑ THE PATTERNS ARE DELIBERATELY BROAD ('*/STK'). The venue defines these
buckets; the symbol is whatever local ticker the venue lists the fund under,
and NOTHING in this workspace records that mapping — the universe screen's
`venues` column is null on all 1,851 rows. A guessed ticker here would give a
bucket that silently matches nothing, which is the exact failure this file was
edited to remove.
⚑⚑ SUPERSEDED 2026-08-11 BY E-14 — the paragraph that used to sit here said
'SMART IS NOT AN ACCEPTED EXCHANGE FOR THESE THREE', because a SMART-routed
order records `exchange = SMART` and could not say which venue it measured.
That reasoning still holds; what changed is that the European cells now route
SMART deliberately — the account cannot direct-route at all, and the question
being answered became cost per USER rather than cost per VENUE. So the row is
matched on `exec_exchange`, WHERE THE FILL HAPPENED, taken from
`execution.exchange` and preferred over `exchange` by `buckets.venue_series`.
`SMART` is still not an accepted value, and now never appears as one.
Record: pfolio-hq/docs/2026-08-10-decision-eu-execution-measurement.md §7e.
⚑ EACH BUCKET IS A LISTING LINE, NOT A SINGLE VENUE. SMART chooses among
everything in a contract's `validExchanges`: the EUR line can reach IBIS2,
GETTEX2, FWB2 and SWB2; the GBP line LSEETF and TRWBUKETF; the CHF line EBS,
CHIXCH, TRQXCH, BATECH, AQXECH and TRWBCH. The user picks the listing and the
router picks the venue, so the blend IS the cost to that user. Bucketing per
venue would split one line's flow across up to eleven cells of n=1 for a
choice nobody made. Venue lists are read from `validExchanges`, not guessed.
⚑ `EUIBSI` (IBKR's systematic internaliser) appears on all three lines and
cannot be assigned by exchange alone — `currency_any` is what separates them.
⚑ `EUDARK` — IB's European dark pool — is accepted on all three lines, and
the live batch of 2026-08-11 is what justifies it rather than an assumption.
It took 9 of 12 fills and appears in NO contract's `validExchanges`, so it
was unreachable by inspection. Crucially the MEASURED commission on it is the
line's own home schedule: CHF 1.50 on the Swiss line, GBP 1.00 on the London
line — the same per-order minimums those buckets already carry. So folding
EUDARK into the line's bucket is supported by what IBKR actually charged, not
merely convenient. `currency_any` keeps the three apart.
⚑ DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: AEB (Amsterdam), VSE (Vienna), BVME.ETF (Milan),
AQEUEN, TRWBIT, TRWBEN. The EUR line can route there, but they are other
countries with their own commission schedules, and folding them into a German
bucket would be the same error as calling a Gettex fill XETRA. SMART has not
used any of them in 71 trials; if it does, `runner.venue_coverage` names it.

EU_STK_XETRA._line: The EUR listing. German venues SMART can reach for it.

EU_STK_SIX._line: The CHF listing. Swiss venues and MTFs SMART can reach for it.

_aliases._doc: Symbols where the calculator class differs from the natural harness secType. Reserved for future use.
